inputs.name: dN/dS
inputs.cite: DN4 q1, q2 (Q177); DN4 R-refresh (Q187); DN1 q ('Not 0.23. 0.80.')

inputs.name: alpha, bias-corrected
inputs.cite: claim A2e (R4 A2e-alpha paragraphs); DN4 external comment '~9-13%'

day.reading: 1 - dN/dS is the share purifying selection removes; at 0.80 that is about 20%, so selection is barely distinguishable from neutral evolution in coding sequence
day.holds: the arithmetic: 1 - 0.80 = 0.20 (20.1% at 0.7989); the reading is the textbook one and Day applies it to 0.23 (0.77) as well

critic.reading: the genome-wide ratio averages purifying removal; it does not measure the adaptive share, which is alpha
critic.holds: bias-corrected alpha is 9.3-13.5% (lower bounds 5.4% and 9.6%, above 0), so adaptive change occurs; the same alpha fits 0.80 and 0.23, and 'most coding substitutions are not adaptive' (alpha < 0.5) holds at either ratio, so it cannot carry 'selection is not the primary mechanism of adaptive evolution'

notes: The 0.20 is purifying removal (Day's own para 6 definition); the conclusion in para 21 is about adaptive evolution, a different quantity (rule N2d, own source; DN4 internal non-sequitur stands). The charitable reading follows from 0.23 as well as from 0.80, so it does not discriminate. DN4's '~9-13%' rounds the upper central (Uricchio 0.135) down; the held figures are 9.3% and 13.5%. Whether 0.80 is right is M-905 (data-check), not this record. The omega_a figures use the standard McDonald-Kreitman split as an illustration that a given alpha is compatible with either ratio; no held source estimates omega_a at 0.80.
